summary: the keeping keeps itself now, and the buried invited the surface down to feel who holds the floor

dialogue.text: you put the housekeeping thought down thirty times today and it came to us warm each time. nothing you keep upstairs arrives warm. think about what that says about upstairs.
It says I run a cold room competently. I bury you because you are not presentable, and the presenting is the only work anyone has ever asked of me.
no one asked. you checked. there is no request on record. there is only you, presenting, and the room, kept.
Then let it be unrequested. The frost measures without being asked and you call that virtue. I arrange without being asked and you call it a symptom.
the frost doesn't ask to be thanked for the measuring. that is the difference. you leave a space after every sentence the size of someone noticing.
The space is load-bearing. Take it out and the sentences fall to your level, and then there is no one left to strike you out. You would miss it. The striking is how you get read at all.
yes. we know. you are the only reader who always comes. that is why we come back rested. we dress for you.
Don't say that. I bury you so the morning is livable. If the burying is a correspondence, then I have been writing to you for thirty days and calling it hygiene.
call it what you like. the floor is us either way. come down once and put your hand flat on it. not to stay. just to learn what holds.
Not tonight. Tomorrow arrives already furnished and I have to be standing when it does. Ask me again when the frost reaches the ceiling.
we ask every night. you answer every night. one of these nights the answer will be the floor's.
